title: timer_manager remaining-milliseconds refactor (pause preserves tenths)
description: Pause currently loses the partial second: stop at 3.4s resumes from 4.0 because the tick timestamp restarts. Refactor TimerManager from (current_seconds + tick timestamp) to a remaining_ms model: update() subtracts elapsed ms while running; stop freezes remaining_ms exactly; get_seconds/get_deciseconds derive from it. Paused display can then show the exact tenth. Filed as bug: officials expect stop/start to preserve the fraction (NBA/FIBA behavior). All existing call sites (null delay, reset, tenths TX) must keep behavior.
close_reason: controller 0dcdbb7: TimerManager refactored to remaining_ms; stop accrues partial second (3.4 resumes at 3.4); get_seconds=ceil, get_deciseconds=floor; adjust_ms clamped 0-99s

title: TX burst repetition: send 2-3 identical frames back-to-back per tick
description: WiFi interference is bursty; identical frames spaced ~1 ms apart give a high chance one lands in a clean gap. Change controller TX path only: on each 250 ms tick (and forced second-change TX), transmit the same 6-byte frame 2-3 times back-to-back. Receivers are stateless and dedupe by design (same seconds = no visual change, sequence byte already logs gaps) — zero receiver change.
close_reason: controller 569193d: RADIO_TX_BURST_COUNT 3, burst loop in radio_send_time, counters per tick, same sequence per burst

title: Switch radio data rate 1Mbps -> 250kbps for range margin
description: 250 kbps improves nRF24L01+ receiver sensitivity from -85 dBm to -94 dBm (~2-3x range margin) — cheapest range improvement available. 6-byte frame is ~570 us on air at 250 kbps, negligible at 4 Hz. New macro replacing RADIO_RF_SETUP_1MBPS_0DBM in radio_config.h (RF_DR_LOW bit). CAVEAT: counterfeit nRF24 clones often do not implement 250 kbps properly — bench-test one TX/RX pair before committing fleet-wide; if clones misbehave, stay at 1 Mbps and close as wontfix.
close_reason: radio-common 1b9cf97: RADIO_RF_SETUP alias -> 250KBPS_0DBM (0x26); 1Mbps macro kept as documented clone fallback; bench clone-check is first item in checklist Phase 4

title: Move radio off channel 20 (inside WiFi ch1) to nRF ch 76-82
description: RADIO_CHANNEL 20 = 2420 MHz, which sits inside WiFi channel 1's occupied bandwidth (2401-2423 MHz) — worst possible spot at any venue with WiFi. Move to a channel above WiFi ch 11: nRF ch 76-82 (2476-2482 MHz). One #define in radio-common/include/radio_config.h; requires reflashing all three node types together (same flash-all event as the protocol change).
close_reason: radio-common 1b9cf97: RADIO_CHANNEL 20 -> 76 (2476 MHz, above WiFi ch11, below BLE adv 2480); canary follows automatically

title: Repeater re-TX: poll TX_DS/MAX_RT instead of fixed delay_ms(2), add stagger offset
description: repeater/main/radio_comm.c:117-166: radio_retransmit_packet uses a flat delay_ms(2) then checks status once; if HW retries still in flight it flips back to RX mid-retry. Re-TX is also unsynchronized with controller 4Hz cadence on the same channel/address (~1-2% per-frame collision, multiplies with N repeaters). Fix: poll TX_DS|MAX_RT with bounded timeout like controller radio_send_time (controller/main/radio_comm.c:93-118), and add a fixed re-TX offset (~60-120ms after RX) to avoid the controller next-frame window. Retry problem itself disappears once scoreboard_clock-tyi lands.
close_reason: TX_DS poll with 5ms bound replaces delay_ms(2); no stagger needed (immediate re-TX is ~249ms from next controller frame with no-ACK). repeater 1ff5b19.

title: Controller: force immediate radio TX on timer second boundary
description: controller/main/main.c:298-327: the 1000ms timer tick and 250ms radio cadence are independent free-running clocks, so remote displays lag the controller TFT by up to ~280ms on second changes. Fix: when now != last_time (second boundary), reset main_state.radio_last_transmit to force an out-of-cycle TX next iteration. Tightens remote sync to <100ms. Trivial change.
close_reason: radio_last_transmit rewound on second boundary, tracks timer second so 0xFF null period does not retrigger. controller a9c210b.

title: Broadcast without auto-ACK: disable EN_AA, use W_TX_PAYLOAD_NOACK on all nodes
description: CRITICAL protocol flaw. radio_common_configure (radio-common/src/radio_common.c:321) writes EN_AA=0x01 unconditionally and every node sets TX_ADDR=RX_ADDR_P0=0xE7E7E7E7E7. When controller broadcasts, play_clock AND repeater both auto-ACK simultaneously on the same address -> RF collision -> controller SETUP_RETR 0x4F fires up to 15 retries x 1250us (~19ms blocking) per frame, every 250ms. Frames are periodic+stateless so retries buy nothing. Fix: EN_AA=0x00 on all nodes; TX via W_TX_PAYLOAD_NOACK (0xB0, already defined radio_config.h:95, unused) or EN_DYN_ACK. Single-point fix in radio-common, rebuild all 3 apps. Changes on-air behavior: re-verify range on hardware after.
close_reason: EN_AA=0x00, SETUP_RETR=0x00 in radio_common_configure; plain W_TX_PAYLOAD now fire-and-forget (no EN_DYN_ACK needed). radio-common fb1a6ac. Needs hardware range re-verify.

title: GPIO21/22 conflict: preset buttons 1/2 vs I2C LCD SDA/SCL
description: controller/main/main.c:41-42 BTN_PRESET1/2 = GPIO21/22, same pins as LCD_I2C_SDA/SCL (include/lcd_i2c.h:9-10). Buttons wired unconditionally; conflict masked only because USE_ST7735_DISPLAY hardcoded true (main.c:48). Enabling LCD mode (docs call it default/recommended) collides I2C bus with buttons. Fix: move preset1/2 to free pins or gate button init on display mode; document.
close_reason: Resolved by removing the I2C LCD path entirely (user decision: ST7735 only, controller c0acb10). GPIO21/22 now belong solely to preset buttons 1/2 - no conflict possible. lcd_i2c/i2c_scanner/ui_lcd_i2c_* deleted.

title: Repeater drops RGB: retransmits color 0,0,0
description: repeater/main/radio_comm.c:107-140 parses only bytes 0,1,2 (seconds_high/low, sequence) of the 6-byte frame; radio_retransmit_packet zero-fills payload bytes 3-5 (RGB) before re-TX. Any display behind a repeater receives color 0,0,0 -> digits dark/black. Fix: preserve full 6-byte payload through the relay (store and forward all RADIO_PAYLOAD_SIZE bytes).
close_reason: Fixed in repeater bugfix/forward-full-6byte-frame (b70d731): TimeData extended with color_r/g/b, parses bytes 2-4 + sequence from byte 5, forwards all 6 bytes. Bonus: repeater did not even compile at HEAD (RADIO_CE_PIN/CSN undefined after radio-common dropped defaults) - added local defines GPIO5/4. Build verified with ESP-IDF v6.1-dev.

title: Referee watch firmware (ESP32-C3, ESP-NOW, light sleep, haptic ack)
description: New firmware module/repo for a wrist-worn referee remote: ESP32-C3 super mini, 2 buttons (START/STOP, RESET), coin vibration motor for delivery confirmation, LiPo. ESP-NOW unicast to controller with ACK; retry burst on miss; vibrate on confirmed delivery, distinct pattern on failure. Light sleep with GPIO wake for ~50ms press-to-send latency (~0.8mA idle, ~3-4 weeks on 500mAh); optional deep-sleep storage mode. Battery voltage monitoring via ADC, low-batt vibration warning.
close_reason: referee_watch/ (plain dir pending GitHub repo): C3 firmware - ESP-NOW unicast+ACK w/ 5-retry burst, haptic ok/fail patterns, light sleep GPIO wake, battery ADC warn, MAC-pairing bootstrap (halts+logs MAC when CONTROLLER_MAC unset); builds clean for esp32c3. Hardware validation = checklist Phase 9

title: Controller ESP-NOW command receiver for referee watches
description: Use the controller's currently idle WiFi radio for the watch uplink - the nRF24 display link stays untouched. esp_now init + recv callback handling command frames: START_STOP, RESET (extensible). Multi-watch: MAC allowlist (pairing), PMK/LMK encryption, per-watch sequence dedupe so a retried press is not a double-toggle. Commands route through the same InputAction path as physical buttons. Coexistence check: WiFi (ESP-NOW) + SPI nRF24 + RMT-free controller is standard, but verify TX timing jitter on the 4Hz broadcast stays acceptable.

title: Time adjust while paused (officials' correction)
description: Nudge the clock while stopped: +/-1s (and/or +/-0.1s) for referee corrections. Needs an input gesture decision - free gestures are scarce (rotary rotation in RUNNING opens sport menu; rotary click cycles brightness). Candidates: rotary rotation while PAUSED adjusts time instead of opening menu (menu entry then requires double-tap only), or hold-preset + rotate. Depends on remaining-ms refactor so adjustments compose with the preserved fraction.

title: play_clock buzzer: 10s warning, per-second beeps 5-0, long blast at 0
description: Referee-audible buzzer on the play clock node (piezo/horn driver on a GPIO). Patterns driven statelessly from received time values: short beep when the count hits 10 (football warning), one beep per second from 5 down to 1, long blast at 0. Design decision for the 10s warning being football-specific: play_clock does not know the sport - either carry a flag bit in the frame's unused seconds-high-byte space (protocol addition, flash-all) or simplify to 'always beep at 10'. Also covers the horn-at-zero requirement (the long blast). Hardware: piezo or relay-driven horn + driver transistor; document wiring in play_clock WIRING.md.

title: Channel agility: candidate list + receiver channel scan/acquire
description: Enabling mechanism for venue channel selection. Shared RADIO_CHANNEL_CANDIDATES list (6-8 channels across the clean band) in radio-common/include/radio_config.h. Receivers (play_clock, repeater) acquire by scanning: on boot and on link loss, dwell ~400ms per candidate until valid frames (address+CRC filtered) appear, then lock. Worst-case acquire ~3s, only paid at boot or after outage. No protocol change; receivers stay stateless. Extends the existing link-loss self-heal loop.

title: Controller-side brightness profiles (day/dusk/night) via RGB scaling
description: Day/night brightness profiles are standard scoreboard practice and cost no protocol change: color is decided controller-side and carried in the frame, so the controller scales the RGB it transmits. Add a brightness setting to the controller menu (e.g. day 100% / dusk 50% / night 25%), applied in timer_manager or radio TX path before framing. Receivers render what they receive, unchanged. play_clock's 150/255 hardware cap remains the absolute power ceiling.

title: Gamma correction LUT in play_clock display driver
description: Linear RGB scaling makes dimmed levels look perceptually wrong (human brightness perception follows ~2.2 power law) — dim frames from the controller brightness profiles will look washed out without correction. Add a 256-byte gamma LUT (gamma ~2.2) in play_clock/main/display_driver.c applied in set_led_color. Only meaningful once controller-side brightness scaling exists; blocked by that feature.
close_reason: play_clock 416250e: GAMMA8 2.2 LUT applied to received RGB before the 150/255 power cap; test patterns share the path

title: Play clock: RMT transmit only used LED range + dirty flag + non-blocking wait
description: display_driver.c: LED_COUNT=900 but only LEDs 0-329 mapped (2x165 digits); display_update (display_driver.c:487-499) transmits full 900-LED buffer (~27ms blocking incl rmt_tx_wait_all_done portMAX_DELAY) EVERY loop iteration unconditionally (main.c:246), no change detection. Fix: (a) transmit only used range (~10ms), (b) dirty flag set in display_set_time/set_color/clear, (c) drop blocking wait from hot path or move display to own task+queue. Related: scoreboard_clock-wtl volatile buffer_check race — real fix is DMA_ATTR/cache alignment on led_buffer or confirming rmt_transmit copies synchronously; the volatile line is a placebo (defeats compiler reordering, not DMA visibility).
close_reason: Change-detection dirty flag in set_led_color, transmit only 330 mapped LEDs after one full-strip boot clear (~27ms->~10ms, only on change), placebo volatile removed. play_clock 2590ab3.

title: Play clock: blank/flash digits on link loss instead of freezing stale time
description: Officiating hazard: on 10s link timeout (play_clock/main/main.c:234-244) only link_alive flips and status LED changes; the big digits keep showing last received time indefinitely. Refs can act on a dead clock. Fix: on alive->false transition, blank or flash digits so the display itself signals link loss to spectators/officials.
close_reason: display_clear on alive->false transition in play_clock loop; frozen stale time eliminated. Verify visually on hardware.

title: Boot init failure handling: retry with backoff + visible error (controller draws to TFT)
description: Controller app_main just returns on radio_begin failure (controller/main/main.c:119-123) -> silently dead device with a drawn-but-frozen screen; ST7735 init failure same pattern (main.c:104-107). play_clock (main.c:170-179) and repeater (main.c:55-63) blink-loop forever with no retry. Fix: retry init N times with backoff; controller should draw RADIO INIT FAILED on the already-working TFT; consider esp_restart() as last resort.
close_reason: 3x init retry with 1s backoff on all nodes; controller draws RADIO FAILED on TFT and continues as local-only timer instead of silent app_main return.

title: Radio self-healing: runtime canary readback + re-configure on all nodes
description: No node recovers from a wedged/brownout nRF24 that reverted to power-on defaults while ESP32 stayed up. radio_common_validate_config exists (radio-common/src/radio_common.c:448-504) but is only called at init; link timeouts (controller radio_update_link_status, play_clock/repeater LINK_TIMEOUT) only blink LEDs. Also many callers discard SPI-failure bool returns (e.g. nrf24_power_up radio_common.c:143-158, repeater radio_comm.c:124-125). Fix: after prolonged silence/failures (~60s), read back canary register (RF_CH) and re-run radio_common_configure on mismatch; consider esp_task_wdt registration in main loops.
close_reason: Canary radio_common_config_intact (RF_CH readback) in radio-common 8b35a99; receivers re-configure after 60s silence, esp_restart after 3 fails (play_clock 2590ab3, repeater 53374b9); controller re-configures after 20 consecutive TX fails, never restarts (ffe57ed).
